correctness.rationale: Published unique extension [1, Proposition 4.4] and its explicit table rule give a total decoder for each block; recovering smallest invariant and its strict row images gives the inverse. The number of non-unit invariants gains exactly one per block, and [2, Theorem 4.3] identifies this with the number of proper nonempty ideals. Complete independent raw-identity enumeration for n<=5, direct all-subset ideal verification for n<=6, and exhaustive partition and Stirling checks for n<=8 reproduce the proved theorem, not substitute for it.

originality.rationale: Primary [1] explicitly poses the partition-bijection problem despite already proving the pair-decomposition and Bell count, and [2] states the ideal description without the new block-graded partition code. An explicit pair of inverse algorithms with the exact proper-ideal refinement was not located in the checked texts or ranked research results; the principal serious risk is [3], a plausible unread prime-factorization source. The numerical Stirling refinement is close to a cross-paper consequence and is not separately oversold as independent structural novelty.
residual_risks: The related Rump prime-factorization full text was inaccessible without interactive institutional access, despite preprint/open-access attempts; its recursive classification might include an equivalent partition code.
The new code is an explicit realization of two existing combinatorial decompositions, so analogous coding may exist under another name.
The underlying enumeration database was not fully inspected; unindexed tables with ideal statistics may exist.
The published Problem 4.6 has a cardinality-inconsistent ambient set size; the result is restricted to partitions of the n-1 nonunit labels.

value.rationale: Provides the explicit mutually invertible operation/partition coding requested by [1] after its enumeration theorem, and grades every finite linear L-algebra by the natural proper-ideal count, producing exact second-kind Stirling numbers for all sizes. This yields reproducible generators of examples with prescribed ideal-chain length, not merely a small arbitrary census or negative normalization observation. It relies substantially on prior structure and ideal results.
